current_example.problem:
Which of the following values of $x$ satisfy the inequality $2x < 10\,?$

I. $x=0$

II. $x=2$

III. $x=5$
current_example.worked_solution:
We substitute each value into the given inequality and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

- We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}0}$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & <10 \\ 2\cdot x & <10 \\ 2\cdot 0 & <10 \\ 0 & <10\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=0$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $x=0$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}2}$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & <10 \\ 2\cdot x & <10 \\ 2\cdot 2 & <10 \\ 4 & <10\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=2$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $x=2$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}5}$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & <10 \\ 2\cdot x & <10 \\ 2\cdot 5 & <10 \\ 10 & <10\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=5$ into the inequality leads to a **false** statement. 

Therefore, $x=5$ **does not satisfy** this inequality.
